newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian premier says Netanyahu hopeful on peace.
newsitem.headline: Italian premier says Netanyahu hopeful on peace.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seems determined to make progress on Middle East peace efforts, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said after talks on Monday.
"I found the prime minister today more determined than when I met him in Israel several months ago," Dini said after 45 minutes of bilateral talks with Netanyahu at a Rome hotel.
"He is much more hopeful that things can move forward... I think that a big obstacle was removed with the deal on Hebron," Dini told reporters.

Netanyahu said he was "very pleased" with his meeting with Dini, but made no further comment. He also said nothing about his audience earlier on Monday with Pope John Paul at which he renewed a long-standing invitation for the Pope to visit Israel.

Netanyahu, on his first visit to Italy since his election last May, was also scheduled to meet President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and Prime Minister Romano Prodi later on Monday, followed by an official dinner.

The Israeli leader's visit to Rome came a day after he and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat agreed at a meeting in Switzerland to convene again on Thursday for detailed talks on extending Palestinian self-rule.
Israel handed over 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to PLO rule on January 17.
